mods.what: client plugin (`client/compat/journeymap`, found by JourneyMap's `@JourneyMapPlugin`): nodes of every network where the player has `view.positions` as temporary (non-persistent) waypoints in one JourneyMap waypoint group "CC: Cloud" (switch the group off in JourneyMap's waypoint manager to hide them all; the group and that choice are kept). Client config `journeyMapWaypoints` (default true) and `journeyMapWaypointTypes` (default `mainframe`, `ender_relay`; also `relay`, `uplink`, `bridge`). Only mainframes get JourneyMap's in-world marker and beam, everything else shows on the map only. Names: the device's card title (computer label, Lua title, machine card) or the block's name ("Cloud Mainframe", "Ender Relay"), coloured by type. The client subscribes with the `map_nodes_subscribe` payload; the server (`map/MapNodesService`) re-checks the permission every 5 s, sends `map_nodes` only when it changed, at most 512 nodes; the client filters by type.
mods.tested: server part yes (GameTest `map_nodes_filtering`: owner gets his network, a stranger nothing, no payload without subscription; unit tests `MapNodesTest`, `MapWaypointsTest`: default types, map-only devices, names); the JourneyMap side needs a client and is untested

An uplink on a computer shows a card for every machine the computer reaches through its wired modems (networking cable, modems switched on): the card an uplink on that machine would show, same controls and permissions. Lua bridge widgets accept bridges on the computer's cable network (`me_cloud_bridge_0`) with the uplink directly on the computer. Public CC API only (a listener node on the modem's network).
